candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents a 12-year history of bone and central diabetes insipidus with femoral biopsy diagnosis and prior liver involvement treated with cytarabine — a classic presentation of mixed LCH/ECD. The multivessel ostial stenoses (renal, celiac, SMA) in a non-smoker, non-diabetic woman with BMI 19.22 and normal inflammatory markers are characteristic of ECD-related periaortic/vascular infiltration rather than atherosclerosis. Atherosclerotic disease as a standalone diagnosis misses the defining histiocytic etiology and the composite diagnostic object required by the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Atherosclerotic disease could explain the renovascular hypertension component (renal artery stenosis, celiac/SMA stenosis) but entirely omits the underlying systemic histiocytic disorder (mixed LCH/ECD) that is the primary diagnosis and the root cause of the vascular involvement in this case.

case_quality_flags: BNP of 82,500 pg/mL appears extraordinarily elevated and may represent a transcription error (possibly 825 pg/mL); does not alter primary diagnosis assessment

Absence of renin lateralization despite functional exclusion of right kidney is consistent with bilateral/systemic disease (ECD vascular involvement) rather than classic unilateral renovascular hypertension
